The core operators D, S, I form a triadic reliability framework for evaluating sports metrics. Discrimination (D) measures how well a metric separates players, defined as the ratio of within-player variance to total variance. Stability (S) evaluates temporal consistency, capturing how much a metric varies across seasons. Independence (I) checks redundancy among metrics using a Mahalanobis-like correction for covariance. These are derived from a hierarchical mixed-effects model X_{spm} = μ_m + Z_{sm} + Z_{pm} + Z_{spm} + ε_{spm}, where Z terms represent random effects. The framework assumes Gaussian copula for cross-metric dependencies and uses bootstrap resampling to estimate sampling variation. Failure modes include perfect collinearity in I, zero variance in D/S, and incorrect normalization in metric types (rate vs. total). The framework supports empirical Bayes shrinkage (e.g., for 3P%) and PCA-based orthogonal composites, enabling robust metric construction and selection.
